mbm-0593.clue: I know exactly when the upstairs window will open.
mbm-0593.quote: I was finding the high part of a tune on my cuatro when our upstairs neighbor dropped a clothespeg on my music. I looked up. She sang the missing notes and dropped two more pegs to hold the page still.

mbm-0594.clue: I keep a green leaf in my paddle log.
mbm-0594.quote: We were drifting under the old bridge when a leaf landed in my kayak. I left it there for the whole trip. At the takeout my nephew solemnly helped our passenger disembark.

mbm-0595.clue: My lucky ball has a freckle.
mbm-0595.quote: I learned to bowl on a marbled house ball with one orange spot by the thumb. They retired it last spring. The alley owner handed it to me in a grocery bag. It holds the door open on league nights.

mbm-0596.clue: My first customer paid me in buns.
mbm-0596.quote: My grandparents kept forgetting whose turn it was to bake for the market. I programmed a tiny calendar that draws a bun on the baker's day. Grandma asked for raisins on hers, so I shipped an update.

mbm-0597.clue: I have to ask before I play the last chord.
mbm-0597.quote: My brother lets his daughter conduct when I play the cuatro. She held her hands up through a sneeze and a sip of juice. I kept that chord going until she finally lowered the cup.

mbm-0598.clue: I wore a white stripe home from the marsh.
mbm-0598.quote: I leaned against a freshly painted rail to watch a little grebe. My birding partner noticed the paint halfway up my sleeve. She sketched the grebe in my notebook and gave it a matching stripe.

mbm-0599.clue: I made a pincushion big enough to sit on.
mbm-0599.quote: Our quilting circle kept knocking pincushions onto the floor. We made a long patchwork sausage to run down the middle of the table, safely away from our elbows. At closing time I carry it home over my shoulder like the day's catch.

mbm-0600.clue: I played my best round with a borrowed glove.
mbm-0600.quote: My own golf glove split on the second hole. My sister lent me hers, complete with one glittery purple nail sticker stuck to the thumb. The sticker flashed at the top of every swing. I asked to keep it.

mbm-0601.clue: I owe the baker one good chorus.
mbm-0601.quote: Our son group rehearsed above a bakery. Whenever the trays clanged together downstairs, our bassist lost the beat. One morning we invited the baker up. He played the cowbell through three tunes and never once rushed.

mbm-0602.clue: I put the remote in a slipper.
mbm-0602.quote: On pajama movie nights our dog always lies on the remote. I tucked it into an old slipper by the sofa. He brought me the other slipper and waited for the movie to start.

mbm-0603.clue: I remember a mountain by the color of its milk bottle cap.
mbm-0603.quote: After our first mountain onsen visit, my mum and I bought cold milk from the little fridge. She pressed the blue cap into my travel book. When I open to that page I can still feel the cold glass in both hands.

mbm-0604.clue: I followed a crooked zipper all the way to the dock.
mbm-0604.quote: A seam in my kayak's spray skirt snagged my jacket zipper. I reached shore lopsided and laughing. My paddling partner drew our crooked wake in the trip book and circled the straight bit where we stopped for lunch.

mbm-0605.clue: I ran five miles for the other half of a pear.
mbm-0605.quote: My running friend and I start from opposite ends of the reservoir. She cuts a pear in half and packs both pieces. We meet halfway for breakfast. I lingered over a kingfisher one morning. She was waiting with two brown pear halves and a very good sketch of me arriving late.

mbm-0606.clue: I came home with a very ordinary button.
mbm-0606.quote: A guide showed us the city's fancy carved doors. The one I remember is a plain green door with a button sewn over its broken bell. I found a matching button at the market and tied it to my map.

mbm-0607.clue: I can always find my towel from the water.
mbm-0607.quote: My beach towel looked like fifteen other blue ones. My goddaughter sewed one crooked yellow corner on it. Now I swim toward that little patch of sunshine and always land beside the right lunch.

mbm-0608.clue: My first landing had an audience of one.
mbm-0608.quote: I practiced how I'd wave to the family after my tandem jump. They were still parking when I touched down. A groundskeeper leaning on his rake waved back with both hands and nearly dropped it.

mbm-0609.clue: I keep one bead in a bottle all by itself.
mbm-0609.quote: I made a bracelet for my sister using blue beads from a broken necklace. One bead had a hole too narrow for the cord. I put it in a tiny bottle on the clasp. It clicks when she shakes my hand.

mbm-0610.clue: I learned the bow from the back row.
mbm-0610.quote: I was late to my first martial-arts class and copied the bow a moment after everyone else. Years later I saw a nervous beginner doing the same thing. I moved back one row and bowed when he did.

mbm-0611.clue: I keep the squeaky stool at my radio desk.
mbm-0611.quote: I once slid off that stool to adjust my aerial, and the operator at the far end heard it squeal. We met at a swap meet months later. He knew the stool's voice before he knew mine.

mbm-0612.clue: I can tell our keys apart in the dark.
mbm-0612.quote: My roommate and I had identical rings of keys. I wove a fat beaded fish for mine and a thin beaded eel for his. When the lights went out we made it through our own doors on the first try.

mbm-0613.clue: I stop my watch at the same cracked tile.
mbm-0613.quote: The last tile of my running loop lifts a little when you step on it. After my ankle healed I jogged there for the first time in months. I'd missed that silly clack more than my old times.

mbm-0614.clue: My first weather report came from a sock.
mbm-0614.quote: My aunt took me to the airfield before I was tall enough to see into a cockpit. She let me guess which direction the planes would land by looking at the windsock. I still play that game with her between flights.

mbm-0615.clue: I owe the little blue tile one more length.
mbm-0615.quote: When I learned to swim, I aimed for a blue tile set among the white ones at the far wall. The pool was renovated last year. The caretaker saved that tile for me, and now it sits beside my alarm clock.

mbm-0616.clue: I made a night sky out of laundry day.
mbm-0616.quote: My grandmother hung her shirts on blue, purple and gray pegs. I used those same colors for the first quilt I made without her help. The bright yellow corner is her odd peg that never had a partner.

mbm-0617.clue: I keep a lemon in my best hat.
mbm-0617.quote: I promised to pull a flower out of my hat at my sister's birthday. My nephew got there first and put a lemon in it. I produced the lemon to a roar and now the flower is my backup trick.
